name: Disclosure quality

subjectOf.text: Mandatory reporting does not guarantee informative reporting: anecdotal evidence indicates that advisers can present the information required in Forms ADV and PF in ways that in effect flatten out and sanitize the disclosures.
subjectOf.abstract: Anecdotal evidence suggests that the information disclosed by hedge fund advisers in the required Forms ADV and PF can be presented in ways that in effect "flatten out" and "sanitize" the disclosures.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: anecdotal evidence, the level of sanitizing cannot be verified

subjectOf.text: If advisers sanitize their Form ADV and Form PF filings, the disclosures become less useful for FSOC and SEC evaluation and undermine the very determination of systemic risk posed by private funds that the reporting regime was built to enable.
subjectOf.abstract: Although the level of sanitizing of disclosures cannot be verified, sanitized disclosures could be less useful for FSCO and SEC evaluation and their determination of the systemic risk posed by private funds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: to the extent disclosures are in fact sanitized, which the Author states cannot be verified

subjectOf.text: Under both the bankruptcy and the systemic risk disclosure regimes, filed data carries a serious risk of being out of date and less accurate at the time it is analyzed than when it was disclosed, partly because of the lag needed to collect data before filing.
subjectOf.abstract: It is important to note that for purposes of any analysis of filed data under either disclosure system, there is a serious risk that data may be out of date and less accurate when analysed than at the time when it was disclosed.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463
scope_conditions: any analysis of data filed under Revised Rule 2019 or Form PF

subjectOf.text: The FSOC relied most heavily on some of the most problematic disclosure items the SEC collects, even though SEC data played a crucial role at every stage of its systemic risk assessment of private funds.
subjectOf.abstract: The author showed that while the SEC's data played a crucial role in all stages of FSOC's systemic risk assessment of private funds, the FSOC relied most heavily on some of the most problematic disclosure items collected by the SEC.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097
scope_conditions: FSOC systemic risk assessment of private funds
